AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why are diseased plants not added to compost? (1 mark)
   A. They are too heavy
   B. They rot too slowly to count
   C. They make the heap too tall
   D. The disease can spread to the crops later

2. Which of these is a green material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Dry leaves
   B. Fresh cut grass
   C. Straw
   D. Dry maize stalks

3. What is drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
   B. Throwing water from a bucket quickly
   C. Spraying water high into the air
   D. Flooding the whole field

4. Which of these is a peaceful way of protecting fruit from birds? (1 mark)
   A. Setting traps that kill
   B. Poisoning the birds
   C. Burning the trees
   D. Covering trees with a light net

5. How long may carrot seeds take to sprout? (1 mark)
   A. One to three weeks
   B. One day
   C. One hour
   D. One year

6. What is a trellis? (1 mark)
   A. A tool for cutting
   B. A bag for seeds
   C. A support structure for climbing plants
   D. A type of fruit

7. Why is compost mixed into the planting hole? (1 mark)
   A. It prevents growth
   B. It kills the seedling
   C. It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   D. It makes the hole shallow

8. Which of these fruits does best in cool highland areas? (1 mark)
   A. Mango
   B. Coconut
   C. Cashew nut
   D. Tree tomato

9. Which is an example of caring for fruit plants? (1 mark)
   A. Watering, weeding and mulching
   B. Cutting the roots
   C. Burning the leaves
   D. Leaving them without water

10. Which is likely to take longest to give fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Passion fruit
   B. Mango tree
   C. Radish
   D. Pawpaw

11. What is the young one of a hen called? (1 mark)
   A. Lamb
   B. Chick
   C. Kid
   D. Calf

12. What is a male sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Bull
   B. Cock
   C. Billy
   D. Ram

13. What is the young one of a cow called? (1 mark)
   A. Lamb
   B. Calf
   C. Kid
   D. Chick

14. Which nutrient in eggs helps the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Starch only
   C. Protein
   D. Sugar only

15. Who should be called when a cow is sick? (1 mark)
   A. A driver
   B. A veterinary officer
   C. A carpenter
   D. A tailor

16. What do protective foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Give all the body's energy
   B. Help the body to fight sickness
   C. Store water
   D. Build walls

17. Which of these is used for boiling food? (1 mark)
   A. A saucepan with a lid
   B. A plate
   C. A frying pan only
   D. A basket

18. Which is a disadvantage of too much frying? (1 mark)
   A. It removes all flavour
   B. It uses no heat
   C. Too much oil is not good for health
   D. It makes food cold

19. Which food is usually shallow fried? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Boiled rice
   C. Boiled maize
   D. Tea

20. Which food is cooked by deep frying and not shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Mandazi
   B. A fried egg
   C. Chapati in a pan
   D. Fish pieces in a pan

21. Which PPE would you wear on your hands to handle dirty things? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Headgear
   C. Gloves
   D. Gumboots

22. How does the tippy tap release water? (1 mark)
   A. By a magnet
   B. A foot lever tips the container
   C. By a switch
   D. By a battery

23. Why do farmers and cleaners wear personal protective equipment? (1 mark)
   A. To make work slower
   B. To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
   C. To keep food hot
   D. To look tall

24. Which food is bad for teeth if eaten too often? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetables
   B. Sweets
   C. Water
   D. Eggs

25. Which PPE is thrown away rather than washed? (1 mark)
   A. An overall
   B. A paper dust mask
   C. A cloth mask
   D. Canvas shoes

26. Which PPE protects the hands? (1 mark)
   A. Gumboots
   B. Gloves
   C. Dust mask
   D. Headgear

27. What should you do if you prick your finger? (1 mark)
   A. Put dirt on it
   B. Tell the teacher and wash with soap and water
   C. Ignore it
   D. Hide it

28. Which cloth is easiest for beginners? (1 mark)
   A. Wire mesh
   B. Cotton
   C. Slippery silk
   D. Thick leather

29. What is a hem? (1 mark)
   A. A button
   B. A needle
   C. A folded and stitched edge of cloth
   D. A hole

30. Why should tacking thread not be pulled tight? (1 mark)
   A. The cloth will wrinkle
   B. It will become long
   C. Thread is expensive
   D. It will not hold

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Name three products we get from cattle. (3 marks)

32. Explain pruning. (2 marks)

33. A school wants to make compost from kitchen and garden wastes. Write a plan with the materials, the place, the steps and the safety measures. (5 marks)

34. How can a school without land grow radish or amaranth? (3 marks)

35. Explain why a scarecrow becomes less useful if it is never moved. (3 marks)

36. Explain how domestic animals contribute to food production in a community. (5 marks)

37. Why is tacking better than pins alone? (2 marks)

38. Explain what is wrong with a meal of ugali and salt only, and how to improve it. (3 marks)

39. Give two advantages of direct sowing. (2 marks)

40. Explain how to make a meal of boiled potatoes and fried egg balanced. (3 marks)

41. Describe how to build a compost heap using layers. (4 marks)

42. Explain what is meant by direct sowing. (2 marks)

43. Describe how to prepare a fine seedbed in three steps. (3 marks)

44. List the tools and materials needed for tacking. (3 marks)

45. Give three ways of caring for a drip irrigation system. (3 marks)

46. Describe how to boil potatoes. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The disease can spread to the crops later
   Disease germs may survive and infect crops when the compost is used.

2. B — Fresh cut grass
   Green materials are fresh and wet, such as fresh grass, peelings and fresh dung.

3. A — Letting water fall slowly drop by drop near the roots
   Drip irrigation gives small amounts of water directly at the roots.

4. D — Covering trees with a light net
   A net keeps birds away without harming them.

5. A — One to three weeks
   Carrot seeds are slow, so be patient.

6. C — A support structure for climbing plants
   A trellis is posts and wires to hold climbers.

7. C — It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   Compost gives food and helps water retention.

8. D — Tree tomato
   Tree tomato grows well in cooler highlands, while coconut, cashew and mango like warm places.

9. A — Watering, weeding and mulching
   Care keeps plants healthy.

10. B — Mango tree
   Big trees like mango take several years.

11. B — Chick
   A chick is a young chicken.

12. D — Ram
   A ram is a male sheep.

13. B — Calf
   A calf is a young cow or bull.

14. C — Protein
   Eggs are body-building foods.

15. B — A veterinary officer
   A vet treats sick animals.

16. B — Help the body to fight sickness
   Vitamins and minerals help protect health.

17. A — A saucepan with a lid
   A saucepan holds water.

18. C — Too much oil is not good for health
   Too much oil can harm health.

19. A — Eggs
   Eggs are commonly fried in a pan.

20. A — Mandazi
   Mandazi float in deep oil.

21. C — Gloves
   Gloves cover the hands.

22. B — A foot lever tips the container
   Pushing the lever tips the container.

23. B — To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
   PPE is clothing and gear that protects us from harm.

24. B — Sweets
   Sugar helps decay.

25. B — A paper dust mask
   Disposable masks should not be washed.

26. B — Gloves
   Gloves cover the hands.

27. B — Tell the teacher and wash with soap and water
   Clean the wound.

28. B — Cotton
   Cotton is easy to handle.

29. C — A folded and stitched edge of cloth
   A hem stops edges fraying.

30. A — The cloth will wrinkle
   Loose stitches lie flat.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Milk, beef, hides and skins, manure, or draught power (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each product.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is cutting off dead, weak or crossing branches so that light and air can reach the plant.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for cutting, 1 mark for the purpose.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: peelings, leaves, grass. Place: shaded, well-drained, near the garden. Steps: sticks, layers, water, cover, turn. Safety: gloves, wash hands, keep children away from the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 for place, 2 for steps, 1 for safety.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a box or tin with drainage holes filled with fine soil and compost; sow the seeds thinly; water gently and place in sunlight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for container, sowing, care.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds and animals soon notice it never moves, learn that it is harmless, and come back to eat the crops.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for noticing, 1 mark for learning it is harmless, 1 mark for returning to the crops.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: They give milk, eggs and meat directly; their manure and draught power help to grow crops; and money from sales can buy other foods.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for direct food, 2 for crops, 1 for income.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Pins can slip or prick, tacking holds cloth firmly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It only gives energy. Add beans or fish for body-building and vegetables or fruit for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for problem, 1 for protein addition, 1 for protective addition.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Roots are not disturbed, no nursery is needed, saves time and work (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes give energy and the egg gives protein. Add vegetables such as spinach or tomato for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group named.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a shady place; lay sticks; add a dry layer, a green layer and dung; sprinkle soil and water; repeat to chest height; cover the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for place, base and layers, soil and water, and covering.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sowing seeds straight into the place where the crop will grow until harvest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sowing seeds where the crop stays, 1 mark for no transplanting.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear weeds and stones; dig and loosen the soil; break the lumps with a rake until fine and level (add compost).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Needle, thread, scissors, ruler or tape measure, chalk, pins, cloth, thimble (any correct materials).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fill the container daily, check for leaks and blocked holes, keep the water covered and clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash, peel and cut into equal pieces; put in a pot with water and salt; cover and boil for about 15 to 20 minutes until soft; drain the water carefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.
